_comment: Encoded design factors: what a descriptor value implies for making. Edit here, not in code.
_status: PROVISIONAL. Drawn from Study 1 site experience and general handling/fabrication practice. Not verified with domain experts. Every derived output carries data_status 'proposed'.
_circularity_note: Thresholds were informed by Study 1. Agreement between derived outputs and Study 1 decisions is therefore expected and is NOT validation.

handling_class.basis: Manual-handling guidance for single and team lifts; Study 1 site practice.

rules.note: single-person lift
team lift, short carry
machine handling required

handling_class.max_dim_note: Above this longest dimension, a fragment is machine-handled regardless of mass (awkward to grip, unsafe to carry).

connection_strategy.basis: Study 1 timber-to-concrete connections; drilling avoidance where reinforcement is exposed.

use_suggestions.basis: Study 1 urban-furniture programme: seating, table surfaces, leaning supports, stable bases, steps, paving and edging. All uses keep the fragment whole and visible; downcycling to fill or aggregate is out of scope by design.
use_suggestions._how_to_read: Each entry combines conditions on one face with conditions on the whole fragment. A suggestion is offered when the fragment satisfies requires_fragment and at least one face satisfies requires_face. A rule may instead use requires_no_face, firing when no face meets those conditions. Thickness = smallest oriented-bounding-box dimension; aspect ratio = longest / smallest.

rules.label: Bench or table top
rules.note: flat, smooth cast face large enough to sit at or place objects on; thick enough to span

rules.label: Seat surface
rules.note: smaller flat face, fragment heavy enough to stay put under use

rules.label: Leaning or backrest surface
rules.note: large face, mass resists displacement. Resting-pose orientation is not computed, so the angle the face presents once placed is unverified

rules.label: Stable base or footing
rules.note: broad bearing face and high mass; supports elements placed on top

rules.label: Exposed face, material history visible
rules.note: carries visible traces of the fragment's former life; candidate to face outward

rules.label: Step or stair tread
rules.note: flat, even face on a thick heavy fragment; low fine curvature so the tread is not rough underfoot

rules.label: Paving or stepping stone
rules.note: slab-like and regular in form, thick enough to bed but low enough to walk over
rules.caveat: convexity required; not evaluated when the mesh is not watertight

rules.label: Kerb or edging element
rules.note: elongated and heavy, with one bearing face; defines an edge without fixing

rules.label: Textured feature surface
rules.note: deliberately rough face, exposing the break and aggregate as visible and tactile character

rules.label: Cut to create a bearing face
rules.note: substantial fragment with no usable flat face; a wall or wire saw could create one

_known_gaps.label: Planter or void reuse
_known_gaps.why_absent: Study 1 reinterpreted former pipe penetrations as integrated planters. Openings through a fragment are not detected by the pipeline, so this use cannot be proposed. Listed here so the gap stays visible.
